diagnosis.observed: Agent-to-caller audio is present: fs-media-2 received 3115 packets from the agent (0 loss) and sent 3118+ to the caller side, and the caller hears the agent. Caller-to-agent audio is the missing direction. fs-media-2 received 3118 packets from the caller and sent 3119 to the agent at 203.0.113.45:16420, which is the address and port in the agent's SDP answer. No NAT correction was needed because the SDP IP is public, and there is no mismatch line. Our data cannot show whether the agent phone received those packets.
diagnosis.suspected_cause: Guess: Acme's new Haifa firewall is dropping inbound RTP from 198.51.100.21 to the agent phone.
diagnosis.visibility_ends_at: fs-media-2 (198.51.100.21) egress toward 203.0.113.45:16420. We cannot see whether the packets crossed the Acme firewall or reached the Yealink phone, or whether the phone played them.

diagnosis.next_check: Ask Acme's network admin (Haifa) to check the new firewall for dropped inbound UDP from 198.51.100.21 to 203.0.113.45 (ports 16420 in this call). They should check SIP ALG, the UDP session timeout and the RTP port range rules. Ask them to run a packet capture on the phone's LAN side during a test call to ext 2041.

Found by ruling out: our server received and sent healthy RTP both ways, and sent each stream to the address and port in that leg's newest SDP, so platform and carrier are ruled out. The firewall as the specific cause is inferred from the ticket timing (Monday replacement, only Haifa affected), not proven by data.
